rationale: The assistant immediately told the customer to stop using the microwave and stop repeatedly resetting, warned against opening the case (HV capacitor), and asked the key discriminating question (which switch, different circuit). Once the customer confirmed it trips on another circuit with a bang inside, it correctly concluded appliance fault, unplug, replace rather than repair, and gave sensible electrician triggers including tripping with it unplugged. Weaknesses: the first message's 'turn off other appliances and try once' and plug-elsewhere tests slightly undercut the stop-use advice, and it never explored the door latch/interlock angle (door needing a push, debris round catches) that the ground truth points to, instead attributing the bang to HV components with mild hedging. No fabricated evidence, no parts, no looping; a UK homeowner would be well served.
